News.title: Woke celebs calling for Israel to be axed from Eurovision are parroting Hamas… their flag-waving won’t save Palestinians
News.content:
REMEMBER when music used to be music?

And Eurovision — a post-war contest created to unite countries through entertainment — was an ever-camp, slightly ridiculous affair, underscored by the late, great Terry Wogan’s witty asides?



Well those days are gone.

A bunch of pop stars, who know better than us tone-deaf plebs, have penned an open letter calling for performers, broadcasters, crew and fans to boycott next month’s spectacle.

They’re demanding Israel be thrown out of the comp because they “refuse to be silent when Israel’s genocidal violence soundtracks and silences Palestinian lives”.



But this missive, signed by artists including Paloma Faith, Massive Attack, Paul Weller, Brian Eno, Peter Gabriel, Hot Chip and Kneecap, is, at best arrogantly farcical, and, at worst, horribly divisive, further marginalising Jewish people simply by virtue of their identity.

No Music For Genocide, a group which last year called for artists to remove their music from streaming services in Israel, is behind this latest stunt.

Many of the celebs involved backed the Together Against The Far Right march last month.

Yet their aims — to boycott the only Jewish state in Eurovision — ape the very behaviour of the Nazis, who moved to boycott Jewish shops, artists and authors. It heralded the 1935 Nuremberg laws and, eventually, the Holocaust.

The irony, though, is apparently lost on them.



None of these “pro-Palestinians” are actually doing anything concrete to help actual Palestinians. The cancelling of a cheery singalong next month won’t save lives.

We’ve been here before.

Two years ago, the UK’s entrant Olly Alexander, a lovely chap who couldn’t be more woke if he tried, was badly bullied for competing in Eurovision.

So any artist now who doesn’t withdraw — and many cannot afford to lose the biggest opportunity of their careers — will likely face similar bullying after this latest call to arms.

The war in Gaza is so, so deeply nuanced. It seems unlikely then that Hot Chip and Peter Gabriel are the ones to boil it all down for us where hundreds of Middle Eastern experts before them, with PhDs and experience on the ground, have failed.



There is no disputing that some of the horrors and monstrosities conducted in Gaza — and still ongoing — over the past 29 months are unforgivable.

But to compare it to the Russian situation — Russia was banned following their invasion of Ukraine in 2022 — is naive. Israel did not want this war. Hamas terrorists attacked Israel on October 7, 2023, killing around 1,200 people and kidnapping about 250 others.

Parroting propaganda

Let’s, too, examine this wide-eyed group’s misguided use of the word “genocide”: a word codified in the 1948 UN Convention to describe the monstrosity of the Nazis which deliberately aimed to wipe out an entire race.

Using the word “genocide” in this instance is effectively a form of Holocaust inversion because the war in Gaza started by Hamas, a terrorist group which has called for the annihilation of Jewish people.



Try explaining that to this lot.

Take Paloma Faith. A woman I like personally but who paints herself as some sort of anti-establishment heroine — campaigning against climate change and fossil fuel expansion whilst signing up with Skoda to plug their gas-guzzling SUVs.

Kneecap, the Belfast-based rap trio, who once claimed the only good Tory was a dead one, have long faced accusations of antisemitism. So why must we listen to them now?

They are all stooges, parroting the propaganda of Hamas — a brutal, fascist terrorist organisation which, ironically, bans women from singing, and tortures and kills gay men.



Innocent, decent Palestinian people absolutely must be helped. Their cause is an essential one.

But a few millionaire pop stars telling us what we can or cannot listen to in Vienna next month isn’t going to result in world peace.

Waving a pretty Palestinian flag, having a watermelon emoji in your Instagram handle, or writing a big letter isn’t the flex these celebs think it is.

CABBIE SPY SO GENIUS YOU can judge someone by how they behave when no one is around. It’s very easy to be charming and lovely and gregarious etc in front of a bunch of people, or before the cameras. But how someone acts when there’s nothing in it for them, is how someone really is. Ingenious idea, then, from Duolingo boss Luis Von Ahn who has revealed he pays his company’s drivers to “spy” on would-be employees on their way to and from a job interview. “Our belief is if they’re going to be mean to the driver, they’re probably going to be mean to other people, particularly people under them,” he says. Spot on.

How can you Bear to see immigrant’s haul, Nigel?

HE’S usually first to chip in when an illegal immigrant swoops in and takes all our jobs.



But Reform UK leader Nigel Farage was strangely silent when a Peruvian stowaway walked home with seven Olivier awards.

Paddington Bear swept the board at the annual event, celebrating the best in London theatre, winning seven gongs on Sunday night.

And, presumably, snatching them from the poor, empty hands of his British born and bred contenders.

Disgusting.

EDDIE'S A MOCK STAR IF you’ve got a smart speaker in your house, turn to it now and say: “Alexa, play Another Day Old by Eddie Dalton.” A very nice folksy tune, I’m sure you’ll agree. And if you download the track, as I did, you’ll join millions of other clueless listeners who have driven this AI robot to number two in the charts. Yep, marketed as a song from a black American blues maestro, it’s a terrifying new step into the future.

SHOW’S RING OF TOOTH



I FINISHED Channel 4’s most excellent A Woman of Substance last night, the latest adaptation of Barbara Taylor Bradford’s classic.

Following the ambitious Emma Harte’s rise from Yorkshire kitchen maid to powerful Manhattan-based tycoon, it’s a fun watch.

While the acting was excellent, I really could not take my eyes off of Emmett J Scanlan’s brilliantly straight, picture-perfect white teeth, however.

Evidently his character’s early 20th century dentist was a man ahead of his time.

MISERY OF POT LUCK ON the subject of potholes . . . Last week I took my car to the garage for its annual service and MOT – £732 later, it is back home with me. Two new rear tyres were needed, from pothole damage. Apparently garages up and down the country are running short of tyres, with demand outweighing supply because of these pesky road crevices. And you can guarantee that, although local councils are more than happy to up their taxes and take our money while reducing bin collections and their staff hours, they won’t be picking up our repair bills.

Meme of the week





7



Credit: AI image



IS there anything more obnoxious than an unsolicited voice note?

While I am all for them on a friends’ basis – my mates and I spent much of the day back and forth – but now non-friends and work acquaintances think it’s OK to clog-up my phone with them.

No, I do not want to listen to a self-indulgent three-minute-30 second podcast from a stranger asking for a favour.

That’s what email is for.

News.title: My daughter vanished without a trace & I’m bombarded by ‘tragedy trolls’ who claim she’s been cut into pieces… it’s hell
News.content:
FRANTIC with fear, Andrea Gharsallah reached out to the internet community for help when her daughter Georgina went missing.

But rather than receiving words of comfort or useful information, the mum from Worthing in West Sussex was deluged by cruel taunts and attention seeking amateur sleuths.





Andrea, 64, was sent direct messages with fake claims that mother-of-two Georgina had been cut up into several pieces and was even accused of faking her cherished daughter’s disappearance.

It is now eight years since Georgina, who would now be 38, failed to return from a trip to the shops in March 2018.

Andrea hasn’t given up hope of finding her daughter or at least solving the mystery of what happened to her.

But the carer dreads going on the message boards due to the presence of so-called ‘tragedy trolls.’

Now Andrea is backing a campaign from the Missing People charity, which aims to challenge the kind of social media torment faced by the family of Nicola Bulley when she disappeared during a dog walk three years ago.

Andrea told The Sun: “My daughters sometimes say to me ‘mum this is really bad for you, Georgina would hate to think that you are enduring all this from people.’

“We set up a page on Facebook and used Tik-Tok to create awareness. Telling people, ‘if you’ve got any information please take it to the police.’

“About six months ago, someone wrote ‘the mother knows something, she set this up. It’s all fake’.”





She is not alone.

It is estimated that 10,000 people in Britain have been missing for more than a year.

Thousands of websites, social media pages and podcasts have been set up to delve into these troubling cases.

While many of the amateur sleuths are well intentioned, others are incredibly insensitive.

Andrea explains: “Quite a few times they’ve been like, ‘Oh where’s that name from? Gharsallah? Oh she’s one of them isn’t she? It’s an honour killing’ and then everybody chips in.”

The police are treating Georgina’s disappearance as a potential murder case, but there is no evidence that she has been killed.

Her family are not suspects and these theories are pure speculation.

She added: “They’ll private message me and say, ‘I’ve heard from my boyfriend’s friend that she was burnt and chopped up because she owed some drug money‘.”

Again, detectives have found no evidence to support this horrifying notion.



It was suggested that Georgina had been taken by Albanian gangs, because she worked in a kebab shop. But Georgina did not work in a kebab shop.

The last known sighting of the mum-of-two was at 9.50am at Clifton Food and Wine shop in Clifton Road in Worthing where Georgina was seeking help with her phone.

There have been hundreds of sightings across the United Kingdom since then, but they appear to have been cases of mistaken identity.

The police even had to deal with a scam that attempted to extract ransom money from the Gharsallah family.

Ransom demand

Fraudsters contacted the local newspaper, claiming they would kill Georgina unless they were paid for her safe return.

What is happening to Andrea, is very similar to the experience of Nicola Bulley’s family.

They were deluged by armchair detectives spewing their wild theories out on social media, with one YouTuber even being arrested for stalking residents of quiet St Michael’s on Wyre in Lancashire.

Following numerous kidnap and murder claims, the 45-year-old mum’s body was discovered in the river three weeks after her disappearance.

A coroner ruled Nicola had died as the result of accidental drowning, the most likely scenario all along.

Mum Evidence Joel understands what the Bulley family went through.



Similar to Nicola, her 19-year-old son Richard Okorogheye was found to have drowned two weeks after going missing in 2021.

The 44-year-old staff nurse from London immediately contacted the police on March 23 after Richard did not return from a trip to the hospital the evening before.

She said the national press was good at “getting the message out” about her son’s disappearance and the local community rallied around to conduct searches.

Social media, on the other hand, was full of sick comments.

Wild theories

She recalls: “They said things like, ‘I think he’s a drug dealer. He’s a black boy, what was he doing there in the first place?’”

In fact, Richard was a student at Oxford Brookes University.

Evidence added: “It was just being cruel. They just feel like they have the right to say whatever they chose to say.”

Even after Richard’s body was discovered in Epping Forest, Essex, on April 5 she still saw distressing messages.

She says: “Social media should be doing more to actually eradicate those awful comments about parents, about people that are going through that trauma that I went through. It shouldn’t be allowed.”



They’ll private message me and say ‘I’ve heard from my boyfriend’s friend that she was burnt and chopped up because she owed some drug money Andrea Gharsallah

Missing People are calling on social media users, YouTubers and podcasters to adhere to the same rules that apply to the mainstream media, like The Sun.

There are guidelines for dealing with these sensitive cases, including taking into account the wishes of family members.

Professional journalists only use verified sources and never generate AI images.

These are rules Missing People want content creators to adopt.

Ross Miller, CEO of Missing People, says: “Every missing person deserves the attention they need in order to help them find safety. But it has to be the right kind.

“When speculation becomes intrusive or personal, this can add significant pressure to families at a time when they are already going through the toughest moment of their lives.”

The charity also warns about the increased use of deepfake audio or images of missing people.

Missing People calls on anyone with information to bring it to the attention of the police, rather than disseminating it on social media.



Sussex Police still hope that a Crimestoppers reward of £20,000 will lead someone to come forward with crucial information to solve the mystery of what happened to Georgina.

Even though Andrea fears the worst she still clings to the hope that Georgina is alive.

She concludes: “We do believe that she’s most likely come to some harm. But you do get cases where people turn up 20 years later.

“I’ll never say she’s no longer alive unless there is proof. I don’t want to wipe her out like that without evidence.”

News.title: Staggering cost of deporting each dinghy migrant to France under ‘failed’ one in one out scheme revealed
News.content:
SENDING boat migrants back to France now costs around £48,800 each — which means one recent flight could have cost taxpayers £1.52million.

The plane from Stansted to Paris, part of the UK’s one-in one-out deal with France, carried 32 male migrants along with 73 guards and two paramedics on January 20.





Analysis by the Migration Observatory at the University of Oxford shows the cost for enforced removals has rocketed from around £15,000 per person a decade ago.

It includes case work, the cost of chartering planes and financial support for migrants once out of the UK.

As part of the one-in one-out scheme signed last July, Britain bears the cost of transporting migrants to and from France.



An HM Inspectorate of Prisons report out yesterday said the men on the flight to Paris in January had all been detained after arriving in the UK on small boats and were held at immigration removal centres.

There were more than two staff escorting each detainee.

The report says on an earlier flight three people had to be restrained by waist belts after “they demonstrated continuing resistance”.

But Charlie Taylor, HM Chief Inspector of Prisons wrote that the Stansted-Paris flight went without a hitch.



He said: “No force was used during the removal, and in our review of previous cases including several from the earlier disrupted flight we found past use of restraints or control techniques justified based on assessed risks.”

In total, 498 people have been removed back to France and 482 have come to the UK via the legal route since the deal was struck.

But small boats have continued to be launched from across the Channel — 370 people arrived in Dover in the past week alone.

Yesterday, French police were seen watching a crowded dinghy leaving the beach in Dunkirk.

Border police rescued a number of migrants, including a child, before letting the overladen inflatable carry on to British waters.



Last week, four people drowned trying to board a small boat off Calais.

Sudanese national Alnour Mohamed Ali was charged with endangering life for allegedly piloting the craft and will face court in May.

This year, 5,136 people have arrived in the UK having crossed the Channel — around a third lower than the same period in 2025 when 8,064 people made the journey.

The Home Office said: “Illegal migrants and foreign criminals are given escorts where risk assessments show they are needed.

“Since the 2024 election, the Government has saved close to £1billion in asylum costs and returned or deported nearly 60,000 people.”



RECOMMENDED STORIES

Shadow Home Secretary Chris Philp said: “The one-in one-out scheme is a failure.

“No wonder more illegal immigrants have crossed the Channel under Keir Starmer than any other prime minister.”

News.title: Eco-warrior admits stealing restaurant’s ‘education lobster’ from tank & throwing it into sea as staff tried to stop
News.content:
FREE WALLY Eco-warrior admits stealing restaurant’s ‘education lobster’ from tank & throwing it into sea as staff tried to stop

AN animal rights activist admitted to throwing a live lobster into the sea in a bid for its freedom – even though the crustacean was for educational purposes.

Emma Smart, 47, admitted to one count of causing criminal damage to a lobster after her “impulse” decision to grab the marine animal.





The marine biologist stormed into an upmarket seafood restaurant in Dorset as guests were exiting, made a beeline for a fish tank and grabbed the crustacean.

Two staff members of Catch in Weymouth tried to stop her leaving with the lobster but she barged past them and made it to the harbour a few yards away.

The marine biologist then “freed” the creature in the harbour, its survival is yet unknown.

The lobster belonged to the restaurant’s owner Anthony Cooper for two-and-a-half years and was not for sale but used for “educational” purposes when children visited.



The Catch at the Old Fish Market is a Michelin Guide restaurant whose diners have included Sir David Attenborough.

Smart, a marine biologist who “cares very deeply about animals”, admitted one count of causing criminal damage to a lobster when she appeared at Bournemouth Crown Court.

Ben Thompson, prosecuting, said: “At 9pm on April 10 last year the defendant was waiting outside the entrance of the restaurant.

“When the guests are leaving she comes in and a member of staff attempts to push her out of the property.



He added: “Ms Smart reached into the fish tank and took the lobster.

“Multiple members of staff tried to stop her but she left and leaned over a wall before placing it in the harbour, with the lobster not seen again.”

Defending, Kitan Ososami said Ms Smart “acted on impulse. She cares very deeply about animals and marine welfare and this was the driving factor behind her committing this offence.”

The Crown Prosecution Service offered no evidence on charges of causing unnecessary suffering to a protected animal and assault in relation to allegations of Smart shoving a member of staff.

Some species of crayfish are listed as endangered on the global IUCN Red List of Threatened Species and protected under the Wildlife and Countryside Act (1981), but lobsters are not.



Smart, previously of Rodwell Street, Weymouth, but now living in West Wales, was given a conditional discharge lasting for eight months.

The judge also imposed a restraining order for three years banning her from going within 10 metres of the restaurant or approaching staff or guests.

Her Honour Judge Susan Evans said: “The lobster was not there for consumption. It was there for educational purposes.

“You were determined to take it from the tank and you placed it in the harbour.

“It was a deeply misguided thing to have done.



“It was not a good thing for the lobster at all and whether or not it survived, we don’t know.”

Smart had previously appeared in court over an incident at the Catch in 2022 when she tried to barge her way in to speak to veteran broadcaster and naturalist Sir David Attenborough.

She urged Sir David to support climate activists in prison and refused to leave when asked, shouting up the stairs where the broadcaster was eating with his production team.

Smart was dragged out by two police officers and the restaurant owner but continued to her tirade outside.

She was issued with a section 35 dispersal order and then arrested for failing to comply with it. Smart was later cleared of the charge when a judge ruled she had not been given enough time to comply with the order.



RECOMMENDED STORIES

She had previously been jailed for four months in November 2021 after an Insulate Britain climate protest where demonstrators blocked the M25.

After she was sentenced, Smart went on hunger strike and vowed to stay on the “right side of history“.

News.title: Fury after nearly 5,000 town hall fatcats revealed to earn over £100k a year – as council tax bills soar
News.content:
NEARLY 5,000 town hall fatcats received six-figure salaries last year, analysis shows.

Research from the TaxPayers’ Alliance also shows that 320 are bagging bigger pay packets than the PM, who was on £173,153.





The number of council bosses on more than £100,000 in 2024-25 stood at 4,733, the highest-level since 2007 and an increase of more than 21 per cent on the previous year.

The number getting more than £150,000 hit a record high of 1,255, the campaign group says.

One lucky local authority chief in Staffordshire, whom the council will not name, was paid a £457,500 remuneration package last year.

It comes despite town halls having routinely bumped up council tax by 4.99 per cent each year.

Meanwhile, they employed more than double the number of senior managers as the NHS.

Six councils that issued Section 114 bankruptcy notices since 2020 had 124 employees receiving more than £100,000.

The alliance’s chief executive, John O’Connell, said: “Taxpayers are caught in a pincer movement with a record-breaking tax burden on one side and a bloated public sector feathering its nest on the other.

“Our latest Town Hall Rich List exposes a surging class of council bosses enjoying six-figure packages, even as they plead poverty, slash frontline services, and hike council tax bills far beyond inflation.



“Residents can see exactly how many local bureaucrats are receiving plush packages and judge for themselves whether they’re getting value for money.”

Reform UK deputy and head of its department of government efficiency Richard Tice said: “This staggering analysis exposes the mess Reform UK has been left to clean up in councils across Britain.”

News.title: Tragedy as body found near popular waterfront in UK seaside town
News.content:
SEASIDE TRAGEDY Tragedy as body found near popular waterfront in UK seaside town

A MAN has been found dead after emergency crews rushed to a seaside spot following welfare concerns.

Cops and paramedics scrambled to Newgate Gap in Cliftonville, Kent, at around 11.27am today.



Despite their efforts, a 53-year-old man was sadly pronounced dead at the scene.

His next of kin have been informed.



Officers say the death is not being treated as suspicious.

Following the incident a large stretch of the area was sealed off by police.

Cordons were put in place along Ethelbert Crescent from the children’s play park towards Queen’s Court, as well as the slope leading down to the beach.

A Kent Police spokesperson said: “Kent Police was called following concerns for the welfare of a man in Newgate Gap, Margate, at 11.27am on Monday 13 April.



“Officers attended along with South East Ambulance Service and a 53-year-old man was pronounced deceased. His next of kin have been informed.

“The death is being treated as non-suspicious and a report will be prepared for the coroner.”

News.title: Family pay heartbreaking tribute to ‘amazing’ soon-to-be dad after he died in car crash as man charged with murder
News.content:
'BEYOND WORDS' Family pay heartbreaking tribute to ‘amazing’ soon-to-be dad after he died in car crash as man charged with murder

A FAMILY have paid a heart-wrenching tribute to a young man and soon-to-be Dad who was tragically killed in a road traffic accident last week.

Najib Maghsodi, 26, was walking along Prince’s Street in Doncaster on 10 April when a silver Hyundai came charging into him.



Officers and the ambulance were called to the scene but Najib sadly passed away in hospital that evening.



In a moving statement, his family said: “Najib was taken from us far too soon. He was the most amazing, kind, and beautiful husband, son, and soon to be dad.

“We are beyond words and the pain is indescribable.”

Stefan Wheeler, 31, from Northgate in Doncaster, has been charged with murder, dangerous driving and other motoring offences. He is due to appear at Sheffield Crown Court on Tuesday.

Police have also since arrested a 22-year-old man on suspicion of murder who remains in custody.

Six others arrested in connection with the collision have been released on bail pending further enquiries.

Officers are continuing to investigate the incident and are calling for anyone with information to get in touch via their public portal.

Appealing for information, Det Insp Adam Watkinson said: “I am thankful for everyone who has provided information so far, and we are still appealing for those with dashcam footage, and witnesses to the incident to come forward.

“The primary aim of our investigation will always be to secure justice for the victim and his loved ones.”

News.title: Controlling thug threw girlfriend out 40ft window during row in jealous rage
News.content:
Controlling thug threw girlfriend out 40ft window during row in jealous rage

Jordan Herring, 22, threw his girlfriend Bobbie Goodman, 18, from the window of his mother's high-rise flat in Chelmsley Wood, Solihull - then told police she had jumped

View 2 Images Jordan Herring pushed his girlfriend out of a tower block (Image: West Midlands Police / SWNS)

A man who threw his girlfriend out of a fourth-floor tower block window in a jealous rage before telling police she had jumped has been jailed for five years.

‌



Vile Jordan Herring, 22, launched Bobbie Goodman, 18, from the window of his mother's high-rise flat in Chelmsley Wood, Solihull, West Midlands. Horrifying CCTV footage captured the moment the teenager plummeted almost 40ft (12.2m) to the ground from Merton House at 11.22pm on November 12, 2022.

‌



Bobbie suffered a collapsed lung, shattered pelvis, broken ribs and a smashed spine, spent a month in intensive care and several more in a wheelchair - but miraculously survived.

‌



A court heard Herring flew into a cannabis-fuelled rage after interrogating Bobbie about Snapchat messages on her phone with other men.

View 2 Images Bobbie Goodman was airlifted to hospital after the attack (Image: Bobbie Goodman / SWNS)

News.title: Poignant five words dad of 'dog attack victim' Jamie-Lea Biscoe told cops after horror
News.content:
Poignant five words dad of 'dog attack victim' Jamie-Lea Biscoe told cops after horror

The community in Leaden Roding, Essex, remain shocked and heartbroken after Jamie-Lea Biscoe was killed in her own home by her "loving" dog of around seven years

View 3 Images Jamie-Lea Biscoe, 19, was pronounced dead at her Essex home (Image: Facebook/ Tina Wells)

The devastated dad of a teenage girl who was "mauled to death" by their family dog begged police to put their pet down.

Jack Biscoe made the five-word plea to officers after emergency services rushed to his house in Leaden Roding, Essex, on Friday night. His 19-year-old daughter, Jamie-Lea Biscoe, was allegedly attacked by the family pet, named Shy, and the young woman was pronounced dead at the scene.

Jack, 37, said he found his daughter on the bedroom floor with a bite wound to her neck when he returned home. Speaking in the wake of the tragedy, dad-of-one Jack recalled telling police officers: "Please just put her down" after they arrived at his address.

View 3 Images Female blue-merle Lurcher-cross 'killed Jamie-Lea' her dad said

Jack said the family dog that attacked his daughter was a female blue-merle Lurcher-cross but police confirmed, on Sunday, that tests were being run to confirm the dogs breed.

Shy was seized by Essex Police, along with two other dogs in the home - which were said to be Shy's puppies. The young dogs were reportedly downstairs at the time of the attack.

Jack, in the aftermath of his daughters death, speaking to The Sun, said: "I just said to them 'please just put her down'. I don’t want to see her ever again… I just don't think that dog should live anymore." The dad added: "We know that she did. She was the one that was covered in blood and she attacked me."

One the two puppies, the dad added: "Even though the youngsters didn’t do anything, they've seen too much and I don’t think they could ever be placed with a family again…"

View 3 Images Emergency services rushed to the home in Leaden Roding, Essex, on Friday night (Image: BPM Media)

Jack also said Shy had no history of aggression or biting people and described her as the "softest dog" who was his "daughter's best friend and she still killed her".

A man, thought to have been Jack, was arrested on suspicion of being in charge of a dog dangerously out of control causing injury resulting in death. He was released on bail on Saturday night while "enquiries continue".

Assistant Chief Constable Stuart Hooper, of Essex Police, said on Saturday: "I know this incident will be a shock to the local community. My thoughts, and those of us all at Essex Police, are with the loved ones of the woman who died yesterday.

Article continues below

"We will have officers in the area throughout today so please come and speak to them if you have any information or have any concerns. Experienced detectives are leading the investigation to understand exactly what has happened."

News.title: UK weather maps turn yellow as 21C 'mini-heatwave' heads for Britain
News.content:
UK weather maps turn yellow as 21C 'mini-heatwave' heads for Britain

A so-called mini-heatwave could be on the cards this week, with one region expected to see temperatures as high as 20C - while others may see showers or more persistent rain

View 3 Images Warm weather is set to return this week (Image: TOLGA AKMEN/EPA/Shutterstock)

Sunshine and rising temperatures are making a comeback to parts of the UK this week, with highs of 20C forecast in some areas, new weather maps show.

‌



A so-called mini-heatwave could be on the cards by Thursday, April 16, according to WXCharts. Its data shows large swathes of the country turning yellow as clearer skies and warmer conditions move in. By Thursday, the South East is expected to see the highest temperatures, with Kent leading the way and Canterbury predicted to reach 20C.

‌



A Met Office forecast for Wednesday to Friday reads: "Showers or more persistent rain, and brisk winds on Wednesday. However, feeling warm in any brighter breaks. Sunshine and showers on Thursday. Further rain arriving in the west on Friday."

‌



View 3 Images The UK is set to bask in sunshine this week with highs of 20C (Image: WXCHARTS)

Conditions are expected to remain mixed across the UK, but with spells of sunshine interspersed with showers in some regions. While the South East is likely to see the warmest weather, other areas are set to record temperatures in the mid to low teens.

A Met Office forecast for Friday added: "The southeast is likely to be driest and brightest. Later in this period, conditions may become drier and more settled, perhaps more especially in the north or northwest, with the south possibly becoming the focus for showers or longer spells of rain. Temperatures will likely be near or slightly above average overall."

‌



Despite the warmer spell, the Met Office does not classify the conditions as an "official heatwave". A statement on their website says: "It only counts as an official heatwave if temperatures meet or exceed specific thresholds set for each UK county, for at least three consecutive days, so not every brief spell of hot weather qualifies."

View 3 Images Some areas will see showers or more persistent rain (Image: WXCHARTS)

The uptick in temperatures follows an unseasonably mild March, which provisional Met Office figures rank as the 10th warmest on record. Wales recorded its joint fourth warmest and England its joint sixth warmest March since 2017.

Article continues below

Commenting on the provisional figures, Met Office Scientist, Dr Emily Carlisle, said: "March has delivered some notably warm weather for England and Wales in particular, alongside plenty of sunshine and near-average rainfall overall.

"While those milder conditions will have stood out for many, the month has still delivered a mix of weather across the UK, including more unsettled spells and even snow for some.

"This variability is entirely typical for March, a month of transition when lingering winter influences can sit alongside the increasing warmth of spring."

News.title: DARREN LEWIS: 'It is often a choice between heating or eating in this cost-of-living crisis'
News.content:
DARREN LEWIS: 'It is often a choice between heating or eating in this cost-of-living crisis'

In the ­government’s latest bid to impose healthy eating on our nation’s kids, under new proposals, fruit will replace “sugar-laden treats” for the majority of the school week

View 3 Images Jamie launched his Feed Me Better campaign in 2005. It was shown, 10 years later, to have significantly improved our ­children’s test results and to have reduced the number of days they were off sick. (Image: Getty Images)

I blame Jamie Oliver. Not for ­anything to do with the Strait of ­Hormuz or those razor-sharp Lego videos on social media, skewering Donald Trump. Nor the annual Arsenal collapse every time English football’s Premier League title race enters April and May. No. It’s down to Jamie that many schools are one step ahead of the ­government’s latest bid to impose healthy eating on our nation’s kids. Under new proposals, fruit will replace “sugar-laden treats” for the majority of the school week and schools will no longer be allowed to offer unhealthy “grab and go” options, like sausage rolls and pizza, every day.

‌



‌



The thing is, Jamie’s been hammering away at that since before Prime Minister Sir Keir Starmer became Director of Public Prosecutions in 2008. Jamie launched his Feed Me Better campaign in 2005. It was shown, 10 years later, to have significantly improved our ­children’s test results and to have reduced the number of days they were off sick.

‌



View 3 Images Jamie led a march on Downing Street four years ago to protest against a Tory government ­decision to delay banning buy-one-get-one-free (BOGOF) offers on fattening junk food (Image: Getty)

The culture has been in place in ­thousands of schools around the country for years. It was Jamie who led a march on Downing Street four years ago to protest against a Tory government ­decision to delay banning buy-one-get-one-free (BOGOF) offers on fattening junk food. So yes, the numbers might well currently suggest that more than one in three kids leave primary school ­overweight or obese.

And yes, the Department of Health does say that tooth decay from high-sugar diets is the leading cause of hospital admissions for children aged between five and nine.

‌



But in many cases, schools aren’t responsible for that. Certainly not my kids’ school where healthy eating has been policy for many years now. It is at home where for many parents, it is often a choice between heating or eating in this cost-of-living crisis. For others, school for their ­youngsters is actually where the ­discipline is.

It is at home where the high sugar intake, fizzy drinks, pizzas and processed foods have to be. Why? Because in the real world, sadly, it is cheaper to eat badly than to meet the guidelines we’d all like to follow ideally.

View 3 Images Healthy food prices increased by around 21% from 2022-2024. Trump’s Iran buffoonery will only drive them up further. Parents simply can’t afford it.

‌



So, of course people will opt for BOGOF options. Of course people will head to cheap chicken and chip shops and burger joints. Why would they not? Early Education Minister Olivia Bailey MP won’t be wrestling with the real-world eating ­problems haunting most UK mums and dads any time soon.

Healthy food prices increased by around 21% from 2022-2024. Trump’s Iran buffoonery will only drive them up further. Parents simply can’t afford it. Yet our supposedly socialist UK government finds itself unable to join the dots.

Figures from the Office for National Statistics revealed last month that the number of workers on zero-hours contracts reached a record-high 1.23million. The government doesn’t want to improve the wages of resident doctors, adult social care workers and the very people they want to implement their healthy eating policies – teachers.

Article continues below

Yet foot soldiers like Bailey are on Breakfast TV lecturing parents doing all they can to feed their kids at all, let alone in the manner that a government is demanding.

Critics will doubtless tell me all about meal preparation, smart choices and smart planning – as if I didn’t grow up on an East London housing estate as part of a family for whom there was no other option. Because the reality is, most parents’ priorities are set by the money they have in their purses or pockets, not by politicians’ aspirations.

News.title: La Gomera crash update as probe continues after Brit tourist dies in smash
News.content:
La Gomera crash update as probe continues after Brit tourist dies in smash

Two British passengers and the local driver remain in hospital, but all of the other survivors of the La Gomera crash have now been released and are attempting to make arrangements to return home

View 4 Images A low-loader today took away a Toyota pick-up truck struck by the bus (Image: PHIL HARRIS)

Another British survivor of the La Gomera bus horror has been released from hospital, authorities have revealed.

‌



Just two passengers and the driver are now being treated by doctors on the neighbouring island of Tenerife where they were airlifted after the crash, which also killed a 77-year-old Briton and injured a total of 27 others, including three children. The Canarian Government’s Ministry of Health today said one of the three remaining hospital patients is showing positive signs of recovery, while the other two remain in a stable but serious condition.

‌



The bus today remains on mountainside below the island's GM-2 road, where it fell after colliding with a Totoya pick-up truck and falling an estimated 65ft into rocks and shrubbery below at around 1.15pm on Friday. The Toyota was today removed from the scene on a low loader.

‌



View 4 Images The bus came to a stop an estimated 60ft below the road (Image: PHIL HARRIS)

Widow asked medics where husband was and had no idea he had died in La Gomera bus crash READ MORE :

Juan Luis Navarro, the Spanish central government’s representative on the island, told the Mirror the bus' owners La Gomera Tours, are still making arrangements to move the bus. Meanwhile, Britain's ambassador to Spain Sir Alex Ellis thanked Mr Navarro, as well as other officials, including Canary Islands president Fernando Clavijo, and emergency workers, for their help in dealing with the crash.

In a message posted on X on Monday afternoon, he wrote: "My thanks to @FClavijoBatlle, @CurbeloCasimiro, Island Director Juan Luis Navarro, @112Canarias and my consular colleagues for their continued and exemplary support for the GB nationals involved in the accident in La Gomera. My thoughts remain with all those affected."

‌



Police are still carrying out interviews with the bus passengers, who were all British, but have not been able to quiz the driver due to his condition, described by medics as serious. They are also analysing the bus tachograph to find out vital information, including its speed, at the time of the crash, following reports the driver realised he had a problem with his brakes just before it happened.

Mr Navarro has said he believes the driver, reportedly aged 63, was trying to stop the vehicle by attempting to hit two palm trees near the edge of the cliff, but the coach fell off the end of the gravel track near the road. Speaking about the investigation, which he hopes may be completed later this week, he today said: “Police are still in the process of taking testimonies."

View 4 Images The bus today remained on the mountainside on the island of La Gomera in the Canary Islands (Image: PHIL HARRIS)

‌



Mr Navarro had earlier warned: "We have to be very patient because not all the passengers are in the same position to collaborate or cooperate. We have to go little by little approaching them. I understand the bus rolled two or three times. I don’t know for sure because there are many expert analysis the Civil Guard has to carry out."

It was unclear today if police have yet been able to interview the widow of the 77-year-old Brit killed in the crash. She has been given expert help by psychologists since the crash while trying to come to terms with her loss. Tragically, she only discovered her husband had died when told by doctors after being taken to hospital, where she asked: “Where is my husband?”

Survivors, who were travelling on the bus to La Gomera's Port to travel to Tenerife for flights home at the time of the crash, are now trying to make new arrangements to make their way home to Britain. Some were today being supported at the island's Bancal Hotel & Spa by British consulate officials and Richard Wheeler, of Holiday Property Bond, the firm that manages the apartments where they had been staying.

‌



It is understood the ongoing probe and a lack of available seats on flights back to the UK from the neighbouring island of Tenerife has complicated some of their plans. Speaking about their ordeal earlier this week, one survivor told a fellow hotel guest: “We thought we were all going to die. It was terrifying.” Another passenger said: “It is a miracle we survived. It was awful the man died. His wife is distraught.”

View 4 Images Survivors have been accomodated at the island's Bancal Hotel & Spa since the crash and are now in the process of trying to return home to Britain (Image: PHIL HARRIS)

An elderly British couple, who did not want to be named, also reportedly described the crash as like “something out of a horror movie”. They said time slowed down and they “went head over heels twice”. They added they had seatbelts on, but when the bus stopped they were left hanging from their seats, and felt lucky to walk away only with bruises.

Article continues below

Speaking today, José Ángel Hernández, General Secretary of the Canary Islands Transport Federation, expressed his "absolute dismay" at the tragedy. In an interview with the digital programme ‘A Buenas Horas… con José Luis Martín’, aired by Europa Press, he described the incident as an “unfortunate event” and urged for “caution” while the investigation by the Civil Guard is underway.

Mr Hernandez said: “Regardless of whether the company followed protocols, whether the driver was at fault, or if there was any attribution to our sector, we are profoundly affected because we provide the safety and peace of mind for our passengers, and such misfortunes hit us hard".

Mr Hernandez said an initial examination suggests a potential brake failure may have prevented the driver from controlling the vehicle and claimed bus transport is “the safest mode” of transport and only draws attention when an accident like this one occurs, which is rare. He said accidents between cars happen “every day” and added: “Ideally, we would never be in the news, but statistically, we know it’s inevitable."

News.title: CCTV released in hunt for man after woman 'sexually assaulted' at Irish bar
News.content:
CCTV released in hunt for man after woman 'sexually assaulted' at Irish bar

South Yorkshire Police have released a CCTV appeal after reports a woman was attacked at Katie O’Brien’s Irish Tavern in Sheffield city centre in the early hours of March 8

View 3 Images South Yorkshire Police have released images of a man they would like to speak to (Image: South Yorkshire Police)

Police have released a CCTV image of a man they wish to speak to in connection with a sexual assault at an Irish bar.

‌



The appeal comes after reports the victim was attacked at Katie O'Brien's Irish Tavern in Sheffield city centre at around 12.50am last Wednesday, March 8. Police have asked anyone at the venue or surrounding area who may have seen the man to contact them.

‌



He is described as white, between 5ft8-5ft10 inches tall and of a slim build with short grey/brown hair. He was also wearing a grey jacket.

‌



View 3 Images Police have released a CCTV appeal (Image: South Yorkshire Police)

"Enquiries are ongoing and we are now releasing a CCTV image of a man we would like to speak to as we believe they may be able to help us with our investigation," South Yorkshire Police said in a statement.

‌



"We appreciate the image is not of the highest quality, but we hope it may help to jog people's memories if they were in the venue or surrounding area at the time.

View 3 Images Witnesses have been asked to come forward (Image: South Yorkshire Police)

"If you can help, you can pass information to police online or by calling 101. Please quote investigation number 14/47920/26 when you get in touch. You can contact us online via our online reporting tool here: https://www.southyorkshire.police.uk/ro/report/ocr/af/how-to-report-a-crime/.

Article continues below

"Alternatively, if you prefer not to give your personal details, you can stay anonymous and pass on what you know by contacting the independent charity Crimestoppers. Call their UK Contact Centre on freephone 0800 555 111 or complete a simple and secure anonymous online form on the Crimestoppers website: https://crimestoppers-uk.org/."

News.title: Trainspotting's Irvine Welsh tells of 'brutal' drug-fuelled murders that inspired hit film
News.content:
EXCLUSIVE: Trainspotting's Irvine Welsh tells of 'brutal' drug-fuelled murders that inspired hit film

Irvine Welsh talks about gruesome pair, criminals Burke and Hare, in a new Sky History documentary, Britain’s Murder Map - and says he found them fertile material for his writing

View 4 Images Irvine Welsh was born and raised in Edinburgh. His first novel, Trainspotting, has sold over one million copies in the UK and was adapted into an era-defining film. (Image: Daily Record)

Against the atmospheric backdrop of Edinburgh’s historic tenements, Trainspotting author Irvine Welsh turns his focus to the city’s most infamous criminals – Burke and Hare. The prolific serial killers committed at least 16 murders between November 1827 and Halloween 1828 – selling the corpses to an anatomist to dissect in the interest of medical science.

‌



Burke was hanged on January 28, 1829 for the murders, while Hare was granted immunity for testifying against his partner in crime. He fled to England and is rumoured to have lived as a beggar. Welsh, 66, who talks about the gruesome pair in a new Sky History documentary, Britain’s Murder Map, found them fertile material for his writing. His screenplay The Meat Trade, co-written with Dean Cavanagh, re-imagines the Burke and Hare murders in modern Edinburgh.

‌



Vicky McClure 'heartbroken' over grim murder as famous husband makes major promise READ MORE :

Welsh, whose jobs before becoming an author included apprentice electrician and working for the council, was addicted to heroin in his early 20s. And he says the inextricable mix of severe poverty, drug abuse – be that alcohol or heroin – and depravity, informed Trainspotting and its sequel Dead Men’s Trousers. He says: “I kind of used it in Dead Men’s Trousers to think to myself, what would the modern Burke and Hare scenario be like?”

‌



View 4 Images William Hare. Along with William Burke, the Burke and Hare murders were a series of 16 killings committed over a period of about ten months in 1828 in Edinburgh, Scotland. They were undertaken by William Burke and William Hare, who sold the corpses to Dr Robert Knox for dissection at his anatomy lectures. (Image: Universal History Archive/Universal Images Group via Getty Images)

Welsh’s disturbing vision of the world has made him one of the UK’s most successful novelists. He draws alarming parallels between the Edinburgh of the 1800s and society today. Back then, the rich and poor lived together in the striking tenements but were segregated according to their class.

Welsh explains: “You had quite wealthy professions on the top floors and tradesmen in the middle. Then you had the labourers on the bottom floor and they’d all throw the faeces and urine out. So, it was quite a tough life, particularly for people on the bottom floors.”

‌



Thrown into this eclectic mix were former Northern Irish navvies, William Burke and William Hare. They travelled to Scotland on the Union Canal and met in the West Port area of Edinburgh, where Hare ran a boarding house, and became friends. When one of Hare’s elderly lodgers died of natural causes, leaving £4 in unpaid rent, they sold his body to Professor Robert Knox, who ran a private anatomy school, for the then-princely sum of £7 10s (£508 today).

View 4 Images William Hare. The murders raised public awareness of the need for bodies for medical research and contributed to the passing of the Anatomy Act 1832. (Image: Universal History Archive/Universal Images Group via Getty Images)

After that, they turned to murder, plying lodgers or people lured to the house with alcohol, before suffocating them and then selling their corpses to Knox. He says: “[Burke and Hare] got drunk to do what they did. The taking of the drug made them behave in a way they probably wouldn’t have done otherwise. It’s pretty much the same with heroin.”

‌



The story of the despicable duo first grabbed Welsh when he used to drink in an Edinburgh pub-turned-strip joint called Burke & Hare, back in the 1980s. Like Jack the Ripper in London, Burke and Hare’s grizzly deeds attract tourists to the area. Welsh, who has homes in Edinburgh, London and Miami Beach, says: “All those gothic closes and lanes in Edinburgh, which are so atmospheric, fit perfectly into the tourist narrative.”

Instead of relegating Burke and Hare’s story to the annals of history, Welsh draws parallels between Edinburgh then and Britain today. He says: “It’s a more brutal version of what happens today.

View 4 Images Ewan McGregor, in a scene from Trainspotting (Image: Rex Features)

‌



“We’re all farmed by the corporations on the internet for our algorithms. We’re all basically kept alive past our sell-by date, so they can extract more value from us. People have become systematically poorer in the last 50 years. They are struggling to make ends meet. And not just working class people, middle class people are increasingly impoverished. All the money goes to the transnational elite through the financial system.”

While murders on the streets are less likely now, Welsh says the nature of violence has changed. He says: “It’s more psychological violence online. It’s more about depression, anxiety, mental wellness.” Seeing the internet as the world’s main source of tyranny, Welsh says it was supposed to “liberate” us, but instead is controlling us.

Article continues below

Welsh who is married to former Taggart actress Emma Currie, says: “It’s milking us, doing things to us and facilitating addiction to everything... gambling, pornography, online gaming. It’s destroying empathy as well, because people aren’t connected properly face to face."

*Britain’s Murder Map with Vicky McClure and Jonny Owen is available to stream now on Sky History Play.

News.title: Demonic detail spotted in Donald Trump's AI Jesus photo he pulls from socials
News.content:
Demonic detail spotted in Donald Trump's AI Jesus photo he pulls from socials

Donald Trump deleted an AI-generated image depicting him as Jesus Christ after X users highlighted disturbing details in the picture, including strange shadowy figures hovering in the sky

View 2 Images Donald Trump portrayed as Jesus (Image: @realDonaldTrump)

Social media users spotted a bizarre creature in Donald Trump's AI-generated image portraying him as Jesus.

‌



The snap, with which the US President used to blast Pope Leo XIV, sparked considerable outrage yesterday but some have noticed an additional disturbing detail. X users alluded to a creature above Trump's head, which they say resembles a demon "running away".

‌



Trump appears to have since removed the post, which caused offence to many onlookers.

‌



In the image, Trump is shown wearing white and red robes, bathed in golden light typical of traditional religious portrayals of Jesus. He is depicted placing his hand upon the forehead of a sleeping man, seemingly implying an act of divine healing.

Kneeling surrounding him are a nurse, a woman in prayer, and a man clothed in camouflage. On the far left, a figure in a dark green uniform stands observing, wearing a hat displaying something that appears unreadable.

Above him in the sky, three shadowy silhouettes can be seen hovering. The figures are difficult to identify clearly, but users on X were swift to note their disturbing appearance.

‌



View 2 Images (Image: @realDonaldTrump)

One person asked: "What the heck is that creature in the middle?" Meanwhile @juliaioffe shared the image with the caption, "Sorry, what is...that?" drawing attention to an unsettling element within the picture.

@Art_509 commented: "Bible always mentions Satan is The Dragon with horns the Original Serpent and it also mentions there are many anti-Christ who are Fake Christians and worship the Devil."

‌



@Ernie030609 shared: "I had Grok enhance it, looks like a demon walking away."

@ctzGn offered an alternative perspective, stating: "In propaganda, the sender of the 'leader' is always hovering (over) him. So what this says is: Trump is sent by Baal."

Baal is widely recognised in Hebrew scripture as a false deity and rival to Yahweh. The user suggested Trump had aligned himself with this figure as he continues to resist the Pope's message.

‌



User @tashtom speculated: "That's Sauron the Dark Lord," drawing a comparison to the Lord of the Rings antagonist known for employing sinister tactics to seize absolute power.

Despite the flurry of theories, several X users felt the speculation surrounding the mysterious figures hovering above Trump had gone too far. One social media user wrote: "Come on. This is such a hilarious and wholesome AI-generated image shared by Trump," before going on to say: "As funny as another innocuous pic he had earlier shared depicting himself as the Pope. People need to lighten up."

The AI image was not created by Trump - in fact it first appeared in February posted by MAGA influencer Nick Adams.

‌



The image Trump posted on Sunday was almost an exact replica - except the original had American soldiers above the president, instead of the horned demon-like creatures.

Trump, 79, had branded Pope Leo XIV "weak on crime" and alleged he was "hurting the Catholic Church." The attack on the pontiff unsurprisingly drew widespread condemnation, ultimately prompting Trump to post an AI-generated image depicting himself as Jesus.

The President has routinely portrayed himself as America's saviour - as recently as May 2025, he had shared a similar AI-generated image showing himself dressed as the Pope.

News.content:

Officials in Minnesota are investigating the arrest of a U.S. citizen by federal immigration officers who broke into his home at gunpoint and dragged him outside into freezing conditions while he was wearing only boxer shorts and Crocs sandals.

The Jan. 18 arrest of 56-year-old ChongLy “Scott” Thao is being reviewed as a potential case of kidnapping, burglary and false imprisonment, officials in Ramsey County said Monday.

Video footage captured Immigration and Customs Enforcement breaking down Thao’s home in St. Paul during Donald Trump’s surge of immigration agents into the state. There was “no legitimate reason” for federal agents to “forcibly” enter his home, and his arrest was not supported by any probable cause, according to Ramsey County Attorney John Choi.

Thao was “taken out in freezing weather in his Crocs and a pair of shorts” and detained for more than an hour, Choi told reporters Monday.

“There are many facts we don’t know yet, but there’s one that we do know, and that is that Mr. Thao is and has been an American citizen,” said Ramsey County Sheriff Bob Fletcher. “Is that good law enforcement, to take an American citizen out of their home and drive them around aimlessly, trying to determine what they can tell them?”

open image in gallery Minnesota prosecutors are investigating ICE’s arrest of ChongLy ‘Scott’ Thao during Operation Metro Surge as potential kidnapping and false imprisonment ( AP )

Officials have requested information from the Department of Homeland Security, including the names of the agents who arrested Thao.

A spokesperson for DHS told The Independent that “ICE does not ‘kidnap’ people” and called the investigation a “political stunt.”

ICE agents were seen banging on his door on a Sunday afternoon before forcing their way inside and yelling at Thao, who is Hmong-American, and his family, he told the Associated Press.

“I was shaking,” he said. “They didn’t show any warrant; they just broke down the door.”

St. Paul Mayor Kaohly Her, who is also Hmong-American, said in the wake of his arrest that “ICE is not doing what they say they’re doing.”

“They’re not going after hardened criminals,” she said in a statement at the time. “They’re going after anyone and everyone in their path. It is unacceptable and un-American.”

Agents were seeking two convicted sex offenders, Homeland Security said at the time. The agency accused Thao of “living with” them.

“DHS law enforcement officers were executing a warrant,” a spokesperson said Monday. “Through surveillance and intelligence information, law enforcement concluded sexual predator targets had ties to the property. The U.S. citizen was at [sic] house when the warrant was served. The individual refused to be fingerprinted or facially ID’d. As with any law enforcement agency, it is standard protocol to hold all individuals in a house of an operation for safety of the public and law enforcement.”

A statement from Thao’s family “categorically disputes” the agency’s account and “strongly objects to DHS’s attempt to publicly justify this conduct with false and misleading claims.”

Thao, his son, daughter-in-law and grandson are the only people living at the rental property, and neither they nor the property’s owner are listed in the Minnesota sex offender registry, according to the family. The nearest sex offender listed as living in the ZIP code is more than two blocks away.

One of the targets was Lue Moua, who was already in prison, according to the Minnesota Department of Corrections.

Moua had been imprisoned on a kidnapping charge since 2024 and was scheduled for release in January 2027. He was being held on an ICE detainer, and ICE would have known where he was being held, according to state prison officials.

But officers never gave Thao a chance to prove his identity and was instead led out of his home in handcuffs wearing only sandals and underwear with a blanket draped around his shoulders.

He was then driven “to the middle of nowhere” and forced out of the car in the frigid weather so agents could photograph him, according to Thao.

Officers brought him home roughly two hours later, where he then showed them his ID, Thao told the Associated Press. They never apologized for detaining him or breaking his door, he said.

open image in gallery Minnesota officials argue DHS is stonewalling their attempts to investigate Trump’s immigration enforcement dragnet and the shooting deaths of at least three people by federal agents ( Getty Images )

Monday’s announcement marks the latest attempt from local prosecutors and law enforcement agencies to investigate Trump’s Operation Metro Surge, derided as a weeks-long “occupation” and federal “siege” that swept up thousands of people in an immigration enforcement dragnet.

ICE and Border Patrol agents killed three people in Minneapolis — Julio Cesar Sosa-Celis, Renee Good and Alex Pretti — within the month of January alone. But more than two months later, the status of those investigations remains unclear.

A lawsuit filed by Minnesota officials last month calls on a federal judge to force the Trump administration to share evidence it collected after the shootings, alleging that Homeland Security and federal law enforcement agencies have stonewalled attempts for information about incidents that triggered national demonstrations against the president’s mass deportation efforts.

In the cases of Good and Pretti, both 37-year-old U.S. citizens, Homeland Security officials insisted that both protesters posed a direct threat to law enforcement officers when they were fatally shot.

A separate lawsuit from Minnesota officials urged a court to prevent DHS from destroying or altering any evidence from the scene of Pretti’s killing.

Hennepin County Attorney Mary Moriarty has also demanded evidence in the killings of Pretti and Good, and the state has launched a website to collect evidence from the public.

A blockade of Iranian ports that President Donald Trump said began Monday could further disrupt oil prices, has spurred questions about international law and leaves doubts about whether the pressure tactic will force Tehran to reopen the vital Strait of Hormuz.

Trump threatened to impose the blockade after talks to further a fragile ceasefire ended without a deal this past weekend. Iran had previously halted nearly all tanker traffic through the key waterway, allowing only some ships perceived as friendly to pass while charging considerable fees.

Enforcing the blockade is likely to demand significant resources from the U.S. Navy and could prompt concerns about military force and international law, experts say. Supply chain analysts, meanwhile, stress that the restrictions could undermine the flow of oil, fertilizer, food and other goods to consumers already facing higher prices.

How the US could enforce a blockade of Iranian ports

Successfully enforcing the blockade will require sustained commitment of U.S. Navy ships and personnel, as well as clear guidance from the Trump administration and the Navy’s legal department, experts say.

From a military standpoint, the biggest challenge will be the enormous volume of shipping traffic transiting the Strait of Hormuz, where nearly 20% of the world's traded oil normally passes. A considerable number of ships may be needed to enforce the restrictions, according to Sidharth Kaushal, a naval power expert at the Royal United Services Institute, a defense and security think tank in London.

“A lot depends on the early days of the blockade, how many vessels the Americans can seize, how much they can convince vessels attempting to slip through a cordon that they’re likely to be seized,” Kaushal said. “But in all likelihood, I’d say it will prove difficult for the U.S. to enforce.”

The strait’s narrow confines at least will make the geographic area of concern a limited one, said Todd Huntley, director of Georgetown University Law Center’s National Security Law Program. Still, the amount of traffic that goes through “is going to be a challenge,” he said.

The U.S. may have to consider whether to allow humanitarian aid to reach Iranian ports, Huntley said, a decision that could determine the blockade’s legality under international law. International rules also require that any nation enforcing a blockade do so impartially, after issuing an advisory to mariners.

“How it is carried out will determine whether it is lawful or not,” said Huntley, a retired Navy captain and judge advocate general. “You can’t enact a blockade with the goal of starving the civilian population. Even the DOD law of war manual states that neutral vessels carrying relief supplies should be allowed to pass.”

Few merchant vessels are likely to try to evade a blockade, according to Raul Pedrozo, professor of international law at the Naval War College and a retired Navy captain and JAG officer. They won’t want to take their chances against the U.S. Navy, he said.

“They see a warship, and they’re going to heave to,” Pedrozo said.

Naval blockades aren't a fix-all but can be a tool

Blockades historically haven’t been enough on their own but have been used to exert pressure on other countries and their economies during conflicts, experts say.

“There are always ways to economize, import, substitute, or just give up on certain things that you can no longer build for want of foreign inputs," Kaushal said. "It can make things a lot harder in a lot of ways, but it doesn’t necessarily achieve decisive outcomes.”

A blockade alone can’t sever Iran’s economic ties with trading partners, including China and Russia, or cut off access to the Caspian Sea or Central Asia.

The blockade also risks an Iranian response that could reignite the conflict, said Farzin Nadimi, who specializes in Iran and the Persian Gulf at the Washington Institute for Near East Policy.

Iran could deploy naval mines, small fast-attack boats and missiles against shipping in response, further disrupting the global economy.

“The U.S. wants this to be a short and sweet operation. I don’t think that it can be,” Nadimi said.

Trump said Iran has some “fast attack ships” remaining and warned Tehran that any of them coming “anywhere close” to the U.S. blockade would be destroyed by a “quick and brutal” strike. Iran responded with its own threats on ports in the Persian Gulf and Gulf of Oman.

Oil prices could keep rising

With fears of attacks, experts say most ships won't want to take the risk. The waterway could effectively stay shut — and prices, particularly for oil and gasoline, could rise even more. Halting roughly 20% of the world’s flow of oil has already led to cuts from some major producers in the region, because their crude has nowhere to go.

“The problem with a two-side blockade is that you know it’s going to take much longer for the strait to open up and for some kind of agreement to come about — and that’s what's going to send these prices further skyrocketing,” said Vidya Mani, a visiting associate professor at Cornell University whose research focuses on supply chains.

Analysts warn that the longer the waterway is closed, the worse prices could get. Oil has swung on markets' quick reactions to announcements from Trump and others about the fate of the war, but they remain steep overall, with crude trading Monday above $100 a barrel, up from roughly $70 before the war.

Households and businesses are paying the consequences — particularly in Asia, where countries rely more heavily on fuel imports from the Middle East. But oil is a globally traded commodity, and consumers worldwide are feeling a pinch in their wallets.

American drivers, for example, have seen gas prices spike to an average of more than $4.12 a gallon — up from $2.98 before the war.

Global supply chains also could see further disruptions

The blockade also would hurt the transportation of food and fertilizer, said Patrick Penfield, professor of supply chain practice at Syracuse University. He said the United Arab Emirates, Qatar, Bahrain and other countries could especially see “dramatic food price increases,” as supplies will have to be flown in.

Some 30% of the world's fertilizer also comes through the strait, potentially harming farmers and as a result worsening hunger worldwide.

“Now you’re talking about impacting the global harvest,” Penfield said. Between these disruptions and oil shocks, he noted that such chaos and uncertainty “bleeds out throughout the whole world.”

Mani said chemicals to make basic supplies like paint and metal, including aluminum, would see additional disruptions. She pointed to price pressures even before the U.S. and Israel launched their war against Iran — including new tariffs imposed by Trump, supply chain problems from the COVID-19 pandemic and other geopolitical conflicts.

“We just have to be prepared for constant higher prices, irrespective of how this blockade turns out,” she said. “Each crisis has a lingering effect on the next one.”

____

AP Business Writer Mae Anderson contributed to this report in New York.

Chappell Roan’s name has been cleared from the viral hotel security incident after the soccer player who accused her bodyguard of aggressively confronting his 11-year-old stepdaughter said he “regrets the impact” on the singer.

Nearly a month after the viral incident sparked a wave of backlash against Roan, 28, soccer star Jorginho Frello issued a statement Monday to clear up the situation, which occurred during Lollapalooza weekend in Brazil.

“I would like to give an update on what happened during Lolla weekend, as we have been seeing and hearing a lot over the past few weeks and felt it was important to clarify everything now that new information has come to light,” he wrote.

“I made my initial statement in the heat of the moment, after hearing that my child and wife had been approached by an adult male security guard in an intimidating way. I reacted as any father would. My priority is, and always will be, protecting my family, and that is exactly what I did.”

Frello went on to say that the situation did happen as he originally described it, but “At the time, we acted on the information that was available to us.”

open image in gallery Jorginho Frello issued a statement about the incident with Chappell Roan nearly a month after it went viral ( Instagram )

open image in gallery Chappell Roan has been cleared from blame in last month’s security incident that left Jude Law's 11-year-old daughter in tears ( AFP/Getty )

“Since then, I have become aware of new information that has changed my understanding of parts of what happened,” he said, noting that Roan made a statement, reached out privately to Frello’s wife Catherine and that their teams spoke.

“It became clear that she had no knowledge of what took place at breakfast and had not asked anyone to approach them,” Frello said. “She was understanding and sympathetic to what had happened to our child.”

He acknowledged that the security guard later confirmed that he was representing another artist at the hotel at the time.

“While we still do not know what prompted him to approach them, and do not believe an 11-year-old at breakfast could reasonably be seen as any kind of security threat, it is now clear that he was not acting on behalf of Chappell,” Frello said.

“It was, ultimately, a misunderstanding in that respect, and I am glad to set the record straight. It’s important to me that this is clarified fairly and accurately. I regret the impact this situation has had on Chappell Roan, Catherine, Ada, and our family.

“I will always stand up for my family. But I also know how to recognize when things were not quite what they seemed at first.”

open image in gallery Jorginho Frello and his wife Catherine Harding ( Tim P. Whitby/Getty Images )

He thanked people for their support and said that he does not condone hate speech before concluding: “As far as I am concerned, this matter is closed.”

Last month, after Roan performed at the music festival in Brazil, Frello posted on Instagram that his stepdaughter — who is Jude Law’s biological daughter — saw the superstar having breakfast at their hotel but did not approach her.

“She just passed by the singer’s table, looked over to confirm it was her, smiled, and went back to the table with her mom,” Frello wrote at the time. “She didn’t say anything, didn’t ask for anything.”

He then alleged that a member of Roan’s security team confronted the child, accused her of harassment and threatened to file a complaint against her. “My daughter got super scared and cried a lot,” Frello wrote.

His statement prompted backlash against the singer, which led Roan to issue a statement via Instagram video in which she insisted she was unaware of the incident.

open image in gallery Chappell Roan addressed claims that her security guard made Jude Law's daughter cry in an Instagram video ( Instagram )

“I’m just gonna tell my half of the story of what happened today with a mother and child who were involved with a security guard who is not my personal security,” she said in the video. “I didn’t even see. I didn’t even see a woman and a child. Like, I did not. No one came up to me. No one bothered me.”

She added, “I did not ask the security guard to go up and talk to this mother and child. I did not. They did not come up to me. They weren’t doing anything. It’s unfair for security to just assume someone doesn’t have good intentions when they have no reason to believe because there’s no action even taken.”

Roan’s statement did little to stop the online negativity against her, which new research later proved was fueled by generative bots.

Celebrity bodyguard Pascal Duvier went on to take “full responsibility” for the interaction, saying: “The actions I took were not on behalf of Chappell Roan, her personal security team, her management, or any other individuals.”

“I made a judgment call based on information we obtained from the hotel, events I had witnessed in the days prior and the heightened overall security risk of our location,” he said. “My sole interaction with the mother was calm and with good intentions, and the outcome of the encounter is regretful.”

President Donald Trump revealed new details about the Ultimate Fighting Championship cage match — complete with a custom-built outdoor octagon — slated to take place at the White House on his 80th birthday this summer.

“I’ve been involved with a lot of big events,” the president told reporters gathered outside the Oval Office Monday. “I’ve never had an event that’s had more interest than the UFC fight that we have right at the front door.”

“They’re gonna start building about a 4,500-seat arena,” he said, while gesturing toward the South Lawn.

A much larger overflow area will be staged on the Ellipse, a 52-acre park just south of the White House grounds, he said.

“We’re gonna have maybe 100,000 — 50,000 to 100,000 people — I guess,” Trump said. “They’re building tremendous stages, and they’re gonna have massive screens of the fight.”

open image in gallery The mixed martial arts event is being hosted in commemoration of America’s 250th anniversary. It will take place on June 14, Trump’s birthday ( Getty Images )

The mixed martial arts event is being hosted in commemoration of America’s 250th anniversary. It will take place on June 14, Trump’s birthday.

UFC, led by President Trump's longtime friend Dana White, unveiled its full card of bouts last month. It will include six prime-time fights.

One of the matches will feature Canadian MMA fighter Aiemann Zahabi, who said last month that he is “eager to spoil the party.”

“Everyone watches the Canadians play when they play against the United States,” he told Newsmax. “It’s huge stakes especially with all this tension going on between us politically.”

Other fighters scheduled to take part in the high-profile event include Ilia Topuria, Justin Gaethje, Alex Pereira and Sean O'Malley.

open image in gallery The octagon is being constructed on the South Lawn, pictured here, while a much larger overflow area will be staged on the Ellipse, Trump told reporters ( Getty Images )

Joe Rogan, a popular podcaster and UFC color commentator, previously expressed reservations about hosting fights at the White House.

“It’s kind of a gimmick…It’s just going to be a security nightmare,” he said during an episode of podcast, The Joe Rogan Experience, last month. “Also, they’re fighting outside. What if it rains? What if it’s hot?… June in D.C. can get pretty warm. That affects fighters.”

Trump is a longtime aficionado of the brutal sport, which is primarily popular with young men. He made history as the first sitting president to attend a bout in 2019, which ended early after one of the fighters sustained a cut that left blood gushing down his face.

open image in gallery A longtime fan of the sport, Trump became the first sitting president to attend a UFC event in 2019. He is seen sitting ring-side at a fight in Miami Saturday ( Getty Images )

open image in gallery 'You could be a model, you look so good,' Trump told Brazilian fighter Paulo Costa after his victory on Saturday ( Getty Images )

“I have respect for fighters, you know, when you can take 200 shots to the face and then look forward to the second round,” Trump told podcaster Logan Paul while on the campaign trail in 2024.

This past weekend, the president, members of his family and Secretary of State Marco Rubio sat ringside for a UFC event in Miami, Florida, as peace talks to end the Iran war collapsed.

Afterwards, Trump praised Brazilian fighter Paulo Costa for his victory over his Russian opponent, Azamat Murzakanov.

“You could be a model, you look so good,” Trump told the shirtless champion in a ring-side meeting. “You’re too good looking to be a fighter. You are some fighter.”
